lookbackSummary: From Aug. 29 18:00 UTC through Aug. 30 17:00 UTC, published ChatGPT assessments kept Tail at 19% in normal mode. Stress rose from 77% to 82% as weekend reopening risk accumulated; confidence remained 94-95%.
outlookSummary: Tail remains low before the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, then rises conditionally into WATCH for the first three reopening hours. Gap persistence, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension and session-extreme holding are the escalation tests; two-sided discovery would weaken Tail quickly.

forecast.analysis: Reopen WATCH is conditional on a persistent gap, shallow or failed retracements and repeated extension. Two-sided price discovery would weaken the Tail case quickly.
Second-hour WATCH requires directional persistence through attempted counter-moves. A meaningful retracement or loss of session-extreme control would reduce Tail.
Third-hour WATCH remains conditional on repeated extension after failed pullbacks. Stabilizing cross-assets and deeper retracements would argue against a pathological path.
After the principal reopen window, the base case returns to low Tail if two-sided discovery develops. Continued extreme holding with failed retracements would invalidate that normalization.
If the overnight session broadens into two-way trade, Tail remains low while Stress eases from the reopen peak. A renewed one-way extension would be the contrary signal.
With no scheduled U.S. catalyst in this hour, orderly retracements would support lower Tail. Persistent directional efficiency would be the main reason for reassessment.
The late-Asia window is expected to be lower risk if the reopening impulse has been absorbed. Cross-asset divergence would favor mixed rather than persistent directional structure.
Ahead of Europe, low Tail assumes the overnight range is accepting counter-moves rather than repeatedly extending from shallow pullbacks.
Europe's approach can reprice rates and energy sensitivity, but Tail remains low unless that transition aligns with renewed NQ one-way structure.
At the European cash-open transition, a fresh directional impulse would matter only if NQ follows with weak retracements; otherwise the base case remains mixed-to-normal.
Early Europe can add cross-asset information. Tail stays low if yields, oil and equities do not align with persistent NQ extension.
Mid-Europe structure should clarify whether the overnight move is persistent or mean-reverting. Deeper counter-moves would keep Tail subdued.
As U.S. participation approaches, Stress can firm modestly while Tail remains low absent evidence that Europe has established a durable one-way path.
Late European trade can transmit rates or geopolitical moves into U.S. futures. Tail remains low unless NQ holds near an extreme through failed pullbacks.
U.S. premarket liquidity increases in this hour. A persistent premarket extension with shallow retracements would raise concern; balanced discovery keeps Tail low.
The U.S. cash open falls inside this hour. Opening-auction continuation is a checkpoint, not an assumed fact; Tail stays low unless counter-moves fail and extension repeats.

The first full cash-session hour also contains the Dallas Fed manufacturing release at 14:30 UTC. Event and opening volatility lift Stress, while Tail still depends on observed mean-reversion failure.
After the Dallas Fed release, orderly price discovery and retracements would keep Tail low. Repeated extension from the opening direction would be the escalation signal.
By mid-morning U.S. trade, the base case favors lower Stress if the opening impulse has normalized. Persistent session-extreme control would challenge that view.
Into late morning, low Tail assumes no new catalyst creates a second one-way leg. A stable range with meaningful retracements would confirm normalization.
